findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify how pod-infrastructure failures on the scanner-pod path are surfaced (e.g. PodCommandRunner/adapter raising `ScannerUnavailableError` so the mediator retries), matching the gate-engine pod path, and cover it in the failure-path testing section.
evidence: The mediator distinguishes transient from permanent failures: services/integration/security/mediator.py:76 `except ScannerUnavailableError:` re-raises to let the activity retry, while any other exception at :80-82 is turned into a gate-failing finding (fails closed).
The sibling gate-engine pod path already models this: services/orchestration/gates/gate_engine.py:262,283 wrap pod failures in `ScannerUnavailableError`.

On the scanner-pod path, KubectlPodOps raises `PodEngineError` (a plain RuntimeError) for create/wait_ready/copy_in failures (pod_runner.py:247,271,294) and PodCommandRunner.__call__ does not catch or reclassify it, so it reaches the mediator as a generic Exception.

The plan's failure/edge section enumerates subprocess FileNotFound, concurrent pod names, selective path rewriting, and output-file placement, but says nothing about pod-infra failure classification (absence).
findings.finding: The plan does not specify how pod-infrastructure failures on the new scanner-pod path are classified, so a transient pod/image-pull failure fails the security gate closed instead of being retried.
findings.location: Approach / 'Failure and edge paths' testing section; services/orchestration/gates/scanner_pod.py:PodCommandRunner.__call__
scenarios: The scanner image pull fails or buildah cannot unpack a layer under k3s; the pod never becomes Ready; kubectl copy-in fails on a slow node.
A concurrent transient cluster hiccup during a scan run.
findings.suggested_fix: Have the pod scanner path translate pod-transport failures (PodEngineError from create/wait_ready/copy_in/exec) into `ScannerUnavailableError`, as gate_engine.py already does, so a transient pod or image-pull failure is retried rather than failing the gate closed as a finding; add a unit test asserting a pod-create failure raises ScannerUnavailableError.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify how pod-path failures (image-pull, buildah unpack, kubectl exec non-zero, pod-creation, hung scan) surface as ScannerError and whether the pod scan is bounded by a timeout.
evidence: 'A missing binary now raises ScannerError rather than FileNotFoundError' addresses only the subprocess path
Grounded assumption names buildah short-name failure and privileged-pod buildah unpack as real failure modes, but no handling is specified for them
Testing 'Failure and edge paths' enumerates subprocess missing-binary, pod-name collision, path-rewrite, and output-location — none cover pod exec/image-pull failure or timeout
findings.finding: The plan adds a new external-integration failure surface (pod creation, image pull, kubectl exec) but only specifies error handling for the subprocess missing-binary case; it does not state how pod-path failures (image pull failure, buildah unpack failure, kubectl exec failure, pod-creation failure, or a hung scan) surface or whether they are bounded by a timeout.
scenarios: scanner image fails to pull on the worker
buildah cannot unpack a layer and the pod errors out
kubectl exec returns non-zero or the scan hangs

findings.checklist_item: Add an AC or evidence that pins the trivy `fs --format json --quiet` subcommand+flag surface against trivy 0.74.0's --help (MATCH/MISMATCH), or make the live-call AC explicitly cover a trivy scan returning findings.
evidence: AC #1: 'a scan runs against archive-massgov-pfml without either binary present on the worker, returning findings' — does not name which scanner, so trivy `fs` may go unexercised
The plan itself surfaced one flag-level MISMATCH ('semgrep --error takes no argument'), demonstrating this class of silent-failure bug is present in these adapters

trivy `--quiet` is conventionally a global flag whose ordering relative to the `fs` subcommand can matter; the adapter emits it after the subcommand (`trivy fs --format json --quiet`) — UNVERIFIED against trivy --help for the pinned 0.74.0 image
findings.finding: The trivy `fs --format json --quiet <path>` invocation is an asserted external-CLI surface that no plan check independently verifies against trivy --help, and the sole live-call AC is ambiguous about whether it exercises trivy at all.
scenarios: scanner_execution=pod runs trivy from aquasec/trivy:0.74.0 and the fs/flag surface differs from what the adapter emits, producing an empty or unparseable document that surfaces only at runtime

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State the default value of `scanner_execution` (e.g. `subprocess`, preserving existing worker behavior) so the executor does not have to infer it.
evidence: `scripts/config.py` gains `scanner_execution`
`builtin.py` gains `_scanner_backend` to select subprocess or pod execution
AC1: 'With scanner_execution set to pod' — implies pod is not the default but never says so
findings.finding: The default value of `scanner_execution` is not stated. Plan adds the config and `_scanner_backend` selects subprocess-or-pod, but never says which is the default when unset, leaving the executor to guess whether existing workers keep subprocess behavior or flip to pod.
findings.suggested_fix: Add to Scope: `scanner_execution` defaults to `subprocess` so existing workers are unaffected; pod execution is opt-in.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add acceptance criteria (with proving commands, e.g. unit tests in `test_scanner_pod.py`) for 'only location fields rewritten, not body text' and 'scan output written outside the scanned tree'.
evidence: Testing: 'has only its location fields rewritten, not arbitrary body text'
Testing: 'writes its output outside the tree it scans, so it never reports findings against its own output file'
Acceptance Criteria list AC2 (repo-relative paths) but no AC for selective field rewrite or output-outside-tree
findings.finding: Two behaviors described in the Testing section have no covering acceptance criterion: (a) 'a finding whose location text contains the workspace prefix has only its location fields rewritten, not arbitrary body text', and (b) 'the scanner writes its output outside the tree it scans, so it never reports findings against its own output file'. These are the trickiest correctness claims yet nothing in Acceptance Criteria proves them.
findings.suggested_fix: Add two ACs, each verified by a named assertion in `tests/unit/test_scanner_pod.py`.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State the default pinned image references (fully-qualified registry path plus a pinned tag/digest) for `semgrep_image` and `trivy_image`.
evidence: `scripts/config.py` gains ... `semgrep_image`, and `trivy_image`
Grounded assumption: 'a third-party organisation image must be written as docker.io/<org>/<image>'
No default image name or tag stated
findings.finding: The concrete image references pinned to `semgrep_image` and `trivy_image` (which registry/org/tag) are not stated. The plan asserts pinning is 'more reproducible' and the grounded assumption warns third-party images must be written as `docker.io/<org>/<image>`, but the actual pinned values are left to the executor.

findings.checklist_item: Justify running the published scanner image via `buildah from`/`buildah run` in a (privileged) pod versus the established alternative of running the pre-built image directly as a Kubernetes Job / `kubectl run` (which avoids image-layer unpacking and the privileged pod), or state why the direct-run path is unavailable here.
evidence: Approach: 'Reusing gates/pod_runner.py also means the gate inherits the pod lifecycle the checks path already proved out, rather than adding a second execution mechanism.'
scanner_pod.py scan_script runs `ctr=$(buildah from ...)` then `buildah run ...` — a build-tool path applied to a pre-built published image.
AC #1 provenance: 'the gate pod runs privileged because buildah cannot unpack a layer unprivileged under k3s' — a privilege cost the plan does not justify against the alternative.
Prior art (retrieved): Semgrep publishes semgrep/semgrep and Trivy publishes aquasec/trivy as ready-to-run images, which container orchestrators run directly without a build step.
findings.finding: The plan reuses the buildah build-and-run pod (`buildah from` + `buildah run`) to execute an already-published scanner image, but never weighs this against the more established prior-art approach of running the published image as a container directly (a Kubernetes Job / `kubectl run` / `docker run`), which needs no image-layer unpacking and thus no privileged pod. The plan's own AC #1 concedes the gate pod must run privileged 'because buildah cannot unpack a layer unprivileged under k3s' — a cost the direct-run alternative would avoid.
findings.location: Approach section; AC #1 provenance note ('the gate pod runs privileged because buildah cannot unpack a layer unprivileged under k3s')
scenarios: Reviewers/operators question why the security gate pod must be privileged when the images are pre-built and could run as an ordinary container.
The privileged pod requirement blocks adoption on a hardened cluster that forbids privileged workloads.

findings.checklist_item: State the scanner-image registry precondition (outbound HTTPS to docker.io and Docker Hub anonymous pull rate-limit exposure) in Grounded assumptions, matching the pull path scan_script actually uses.
evidence: scan_script uses `buildah from {shlex.quote(image)}` with no --tls-verify flag (unlike pod_runner's image path which threads tls_flag)
Grounded assumptions cover buildah short-name resolution but state no network/registry precondition for pulling docker.io/semgrep and docker.io/aquasec images
T3 checklist item (c): auth/HTTPS preconditions stated
findings.finding: The scanner-image pull precondition is unstated: scan_script issues a bare `buildah from "$image"` against docker.io with no TLS/auth handling, so the plan does not name the outbound-HTTPS-to-Docker-Hub / anonymous-pull-rate-limit precondition the pod path depends on.
scenarios: The gate pod has no outbound access to registry-1.docker.io, or hits Docker Hub anonymous pull rate limits, and every pod-mode scan fails at `buildah from` before the scanner runs
